observations.classification: source-supported safeguards, scoped to the selected entry or iterator
observations.analysis: The central fixed parser requires 46 bytes and the central signature; the variable parser checks file name, extra and comment before each split. On an ordinary next-entry error the iterator becomes terminal, and the application propagates that error rather than returning a partially built archive. On selected payload access rawzip requires a 30-byte local header and local signature, adds its two u16 variable lengths, then checks compressed-extent addition and the available slice before returning raw bytes. The application maps native member errors with member context. These are source safeguards, not runtime results, verified CRC/decoded size or all possible input guarantees.

observations.classification: qualification of wrong-record-kind claim and connection to historical q2312, not a new count
observations.analysis: Although the fixed central parser rejects other signatures, the iterator specially converts a remaining buffer beginning with the digital-signature bytes and no longer than 6 + u16::MAX bytes to Ok(None). That branch does not itself parse a signature-record length or require a six-byte minimum. If a selected directory tail has only the four signature bytes and the application asks for another entry, this branch can terminate the loop instead of propagating the preceding fixed-header error. This is symbolic source reasoning; no actual archive, archive validity, supported asset incidence or rejection policy is established. It limits a blanket wrong-record-kind claim and relates to the separately recorded declaration-upper-bound policy.

observations.classification: conditional source behavior already related to q2313, not a newly established defect
observations.analysis: The application selects and names a central entry, stores its central compression and wayfinder, and gets bytes from the same archive using the wayfinder offset and compressed-size hint. The shown native get_entry checks local signature and extent but does not compare the local filename or compression field against central metadata; wayfinder does not carry the central name or method. If a selected central entry points to a different otherwise well-framed local record with sufficient bytes, its raw data can be returned under the selected central name, using the central method. This remains a conditional source case: no archive, supported producer, violation or consumer impact is observed. Historical q2313 explicitly says central-directory selection is authoritative and local versus central names may legitimately differ; do not recast that history as an established defect or assume an alias.

The native entries slice uses selected directory start through head EOCD; the displayed slice does not use the declared directory size as its endpoint. The application iterates at most its selected count and can stop at Ok(None). The displayed Stored/Deflate path obtains the raw member and does not itself compare decoded length or CRC; native extent availability and decoded integrity remain distinct. Count, CRC and allocation policies belong to their separately recorded histories and prior review.
